senses.definition: A stooped or curled posture; a slouch.
examples: The old man walked with a hunch.

senses.definition: A theory, idea, or guess; an intuitive impression that something will happen.
examples: I have a hunch they'll find a way to solve the problem.

senses.definition: A hunk; a lump; a thick piece.

quotes.text: "The greedy little bastards! They had a 'unch of bread each when I 'ad my dinner."
quotes.reference: 1925 July – 1926 May, A[rthur] Conan Doyle, “(please specify the chapter number)”, in The Land of Mist (eBook no. 0601351h.html), Australia: Project Gutenberg Australia, published April 2019:

senses.definition: A push or thrust, as with the elbow.
(intransitive) To bend the top of one's body forward while raising one's shoulders.
examples: Don't hunch over your computer if you want to avoid neck problems.

quotes.text: Sandy, you will never get anywhere by hunching over your putter, hold your shoulders back and bend from the waist.
quotes.reference: 1961, Muriel Spark, chapter 5, in The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie, New York: HarperPerenniel, published 1994, page 156:

quotes.text: She rolled over and hunched into a fetal position.
quotes.reference: 1978, Armistead Maupin, “… and many happy returns”, in Tales of the City, New York: Ballantine Books, page 76:

senses.definition: (transitive) To raise (one's shoulders) (while lowering one's head or bending the top of one's body forward); to curve (one's body) forward (sometimes followed by up).
examples: They stood outside the door hunching themselves against the rain and puffing on their cigarettes.
He hunched up his shoulders and stared down at the ground.

1938, Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings, New York: Scribner, Chapter 17,
He would hunch his twisted body close and put out his gentle and crooked hand and touch the fawn.

quotes.text: Danc[ing] Mast[er]. […] not too fast […] keep you[r] leg[s] straight, […] don’t hunch up your shoulders so;

quotes.text: If you hunch your shoulders too long against a storm your shoulders will grow bowed....

senses.definition: (transitive) To push or jostle with the elbow; to push or thrust against (someone).

senses.definition: (intransitive, colloquial) To have a hunch, or make an intuitive guess.

quotes.text: People who are instinctive hunchers go through some such process at every decision-making point of their lives. It is likely that children often make decisions and discern truths by hunching.
